source.authors: Wikenros C, Jarnemo A, Frisén M, Kuijper DPJ, Schmidt K
source.title: Mesopredator behavioral response to olfactory signals of an apex predator

value: red foxes visited sites with lynx scat more often than expected and their visits were longer than at control sites (no scat added)
units: categorical (visits recorded at lynx-scat sites versus control sites, chi-square goodness-of-fit against equal visitation)
method: video camera-trap field experiment: lynx (Lynx lynx) scats placed in the centre of the detection area of the camera at 27 of 54 sites, locations randomly assigned as scat site or control site (no scat added); each site monitored 12 consecutive days; visits within a 5-min interval assumed to be the same individual; visitation frequency tested with a chi-square goodness-of-fit test and visit duration with a t-test
conditions: wild-sourced: free-ranging red foxes in Bialowieza Primeval Forest, Poland (temperate mixed lowland forest, 600 km2 of it in Poland); lynx scats from two captive mature female lynx outside the mating season, kept frozen at -20 C for a few days up to 1 month; experiments started 9, 12 and 24 October and 9 November 2012 (autumn); 102 fox visits recorded, 75 at 17 scat sites and 27 at 11 control sites (so only 17 of 27 scat sites and 11 of 27 control sites were visited), chi-square = 22.59, df = 1, p < 0.0001 if equal visitation expected; Results give visit duration mean +/- SE 31 +/- 4 s at scat sites (n = 73) against 2 +/- 0.4 s at control sites (n = 25), t = -7.446, p < 0.001; Table 1 logistic regressions scat versus control: vigilance OR 22.105 (p = 0.003), sniffing OR 110.769 (p < 0.001) and scent marking OR 26.057 (p = 0.002) more frequent at scat sites, passing by OR 0.019 (p < 0.001) more common at control sites; contrary and null secondary results: the paper calls vigilance the only behaviour influenced by time since the experiment started (foxes more vigilant when scats were fresher), but Table 2 gives vigilance OR 0.850, p = 0.058, and no time effect on passing by (OR 1.181, p = 0.181), sniffing (OR 0.856, p = 0.161) or scent marking (OR 0.905, p = 0.257); prior fox over-marking of the scat raised sniffing and scent marking; marten, badger and raccoon dog visits were too few to analyse; individual foxes were not identified so visits are not independent samples; the only control is no scat added, with no non-predator scat control, so the response cannot be separated from a response to any novel scat
quote: Red fox visited sites with scats more often than expected and the duration of their visits was longer at scat sites than at control sites (no scat added).
note: Classification: behavioural_response, visitation and visit duration of wild foxes at predator-scat sites versus no-scat control sites; the value is limited to the quoted Abstract sentence and the statistics, behaviour odds ratios and nulls are carried in conditions.
